newsitem.title: MEXICO: BMW's Land Rover launches in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: BMW's Land Rover launches in Mexico.

text.p: Bayerische Motoren-Werke's Land Rover unit officially launched sales in Mexico, offering two models to grab a share of the country's growing luxury and sport utility market segments.
Roger Ball, Operations Director of Land Rover de Mexico, told Reuters that the vehicles would be sold through existing BMW dealerships in six Mexican cities.

For now, the vehicles would be imported completely built from Britain, but company officials did not rule out the possibility of using BMW's Toluca assembly plant near Mexico City to assemble kits at a later stage.
"We would like to look later on at how best the Toluca plant could be used, but at present there are no concrete plans," Ball said.

BMW currently assembles Three and Five series models at Toluca and BMW representatives at the Land Rover launch -- held at the British Embassy in Mexico City -- said their experiences so far of the Mexican workforce and Mexican suppliers had been very good.

For now, Land Rover is offering Mexican buyers two versions of the Discovery off-roader, starting at $44,500 as well as the top of the range Range Rover 4.6 HSE at $79,000. The basic Defender vehicle is not part of the line-up.
Land Rover officials did not give specific sales targets but said they expected to import 150 vehicles between now and year-end and increase on that figure next year.
Ball said Land Rover planned to use experience gained in the Mexican market for possible later moves into Central America or South American markets where the company is not currently represented.

Land Rover's Mexican operation is its first directly-owned sales effort in Latin America, though the company sells through independent distributors in some other countries in the region such as Colombia.
